records.claim: Within the selected hXe constructor, the options parameter supplies this.scopedState from options.globalState. The parameter binding is explicit; actual invocation state is not observed.
The same hXe constructor passes this.scopedState as zero-based argument 8 of the Program-bound MMe construction; its constructor parameter 8 is assigned to this.globalState.
In vXe, the globalState destructuring parameter is passed as globalState in the Program-bound hXe options. This is a static source injection path.
The selected Program-bound vXe caller supplies the globalState property of one local startup result; that same local binding is initialized by the selected awaited bootstrap namespace call.
The startup-result declaration invokes the bootstrap export U through the lexically resolved module namespace. No value from a running client was read.

The exported startup initializer resolves a Codex-home candidate through o.ot(), calls uT with it, and returns the constructed state as globalState. The actual home resolver and runtime return value are not executed.
uT constructs s.D with path.join(home,cT); cT is the .codex-global-state.json filename. Namespace s is the lexically resolved startup-requirements module.
The startup initializer returns its same locally bound constructed state as globalState. Separate executionCodexHome resolution does not replace the state-file home argument.
Vr stores the supplied filePath, loads Wr(filePath), and creates a debounce callback using Or. The callback schedules persistence only while persistScheduledForAtoms is truthy.
get returns a non-nullish stored value; otherwise it invokes the imported n._s default resolver and uses null for a nullish result. This differs from getStored.
getStored returns the raw Map value without the default resolver.
set changes the in-memory Map first, calls persistForKey, then synchronously invokes change listeners. It does not return a write-completion Promise; listener throws are not caught here.
update calls the updater with the existing Map value when present, otherwise null, then changes memory, schedules persistence and notifies listeners. It is not the commit-before-memory path.

updateAndPersist serializes behind persistQueued.catch(...), computes a prospective Map, serializes it, and calls synchronous Xr on the main path before changing memory. Backup failure is caught and logged; listeners are individually caught and logged. The special archives comparison branch is retained but not behavior-tested.
delete changes memory, schedules persistence and synchronously notifies listeners, without an awaited commit.
flush delegates to flushWith(qr), whose selected write helper logs and swallows failures.
flushOrThrow delegates to flushWith(Jr), whose selected helper does not catch its write errors.

flushWith clears the custom-runtime scheduling flag, cancels a pending atom debounce, and queues the supplied persistence helper after swallowing a previous queue rejection. The Map is read when this queued callback executes.
The atom key takes a debounced path; custom-runtime state/outbox keys share a queueMicrotask scheduling flag; other keys schedule immediately. Managed archives mark archivesPersisted false.
A persistScheduled flag coalesces scheduled work. The queued callback clears that flag before calling qr(filePath,state), after swallowing the previous queue rejection.
The selected debounce resets the timeout on each call and retains the most recent arguments; cancel clears its timeout and retained arguments.
The selected atom debounce delay constant is 500 milliseconds.
The selected asynchronous rename retry delays are [100,200,400] milliseconds.
If the main file is absent, Wr returns a new empty Map immediately and does not try a backup. If the main exists but Gr fails, it tries the .bak file; a successful backup load is logged.

Gr checks existence, reads UTF8 and JSON.parse, rejects null/falsy or non-object roots, filters known schema keys only when safeParse.success is strictly false, and returns Object.entries as a Map. Arrays are not explicitly rejected by its top-level object test. Caught errors log and return null.
Kr builds a normal {} from Map entries, omits undefined values and calls JSON.stringify. It is not a schema-validation pass.
qr awaits Jr in try/catch and logs persistence failure; a successful logger return causes the helper to fulfill after write failure.
Jr serializes once, awaits Zr on the main file, then awaits Zr on the .bak file. A successful main write followed by backup failure is not rolled back in this selected helper.
Yr creates a temp pathname in the same directory, using dot plus basename, current timestamp and randomUUID.

Xr synchronously writes UTF8 to the temp path and renames it onto the destination. On failure it calls rmSync(force:true) before rethrowing the original error; cleanup failure can replace that error. There is no fsync call in this selected function.

Zr asynchronously writes the temp file and attempts rename. Only on win32, with an Error and code EPERM/EACCES/EBUSY, it retries using the three selected delays; after failure it awaits rm(force:true), then throws the original error unless cleanup itself throws. No fsync call appears here.
Ur only tests membership in Hr. Hr is built from Object.keys(zr); the schema table and imported default behavior are not expanded in this batch.
The selected Program declaration directly requires "node:fs". These are runtime dependencies, not implementations to regenerate.
The selected Program declaration directly requires "node:fs/promises". These are runtime dependencies, not implementations to regenerate.

The selected Program declaration directly requires "node:timers/promises". These are runtime dependencies, not implementations to regenerate.

limits: Static lexical path does not prove an actual runtime instance, final home, file delivery, write completion or power-loss durability.
No original client module was imported or executed in this analysis.
Known-key schema table zr, defaults n._s, archive comparator, logger behavior and the full settings/host lifecycle remain dependencies.
Actual interrupted turn persistence may also involve CLI/backend storage; this atom store alone does not establish that mechanism.
Normal process exit flush callers, Windows retries and original runtime behavior are not verified in this batch.
